title: Admin Monitor
description: Keeps an administrator informed about the whole deployment, in aggregates only: usage and cost across all users, models running without a price, the database's health and backups, the platform's maintenance jobs, the scheduler and the model providers. It never reads a user's conversations or content, changes nothing, and each of its readings of the deployment is recorded in the audit log. Its readings of the deployment are for administrators: anyone else's agent reaches only the scheduler's and the model providers' status.

examples.ask: How is the deployment doing this month?
examples.outcome: It reads the deployment's consumption across all users — active users, tokens, estimated cost, failed turns, the models in use — and gives you the totals, never anyone's conversations.

examples.ask: Which models run without a price?
examples.outcome: It reads the price coverage and names the models in use that have no price, so their cost reads as zero until one is set.

examples.ask: Is the database healthy, and when was it last backed up?
examples.outcome: It reads the database's health: unreadable reads since the start, the last backup and how many are kept.

examples.ask: Did the nightly maintenance jobs run?
examples.outcome: It reads the platform's own jobs — usage resets, price sync, backups — with their schedules and how their last runs went.

not_offered.what: Any user's conversations, questions or answers — or usage named per user
not_offered.why: The instance-wide view is aggregates; what a person asked, and how much each person used, are theirs. An agent reads its own user's conversations only, whatever the deployment allows people.

not_offered.what: Signatures not yet attributed to an account
not_offered.why: They name other users' agents; assigning one is an administrator's act in person.

not_offered.what: The user directory, or any change to a user — tier, lock, deletion
not_offered.why: Who has an account, and what they may do, is decided by an administrator in person.

not_offered.what: Changing the deployment — its settings, components, prices, publishing rules
not_offered.why: The Admin Monitor reads; every setting is an administrator's to change.

not_offered.what: Filling in missing prices, running a backup or a maintenance job
not_offered.why: Each one changes the deployment; it reports what is missing, you act.

not_offered.what: The deployment's usage, costs, users or database for an agent whose user is not an administrator
not_offered.why: Those readings are administrator-tier: anyone else's agent holding the role reaches only the scheduler's and the model providers' status.
